nieuw.titel: Choose fast, mobile chaff that usually costs under 100 points
nieuw.tekst: When choosing chaff, check speed, mobility and cost first. The speaker suggests under 100 points and movement seven or above, with flying, skirmishing or reserve move as useful bonuses.
nieuw.waarom: He says chaff needs speed to get into position ahead of the opponent. It also needs to be cheap because it is likely to die.
nieuw.wanneerNiet: He allows more expensive chaff, including some Elf units, but says a unit over 100 points needs a good return to justify the investment.

bronnen.citaat: Under 100 points, let's say movement seven and above

extraCitaten.citaat: you really have to get a good return back from a unit

nieuw.titel: Prefer chaff that can fulfil multiple roles
nieuw.tekst: The speaker rates chaff that can perform multiple roles particularly highly. Look for units that can serve as deployment drops, redirectors or threats to vulnerable targets.
nieuw.waarom: In his view, versatility is where chaff units shine.
nieuw.voorbeeld: He describes Giant Rats as cheap deployment drops that can also become speed bumps. He also describes a Great Eagle redirecting units or killing a war machine.

bronnen.citaat: If they can fulfill multiple roles they are S tier chaff unit.

nieuw.titel: Deploy cheap chaff before committing your key units
nieuw.tekst: Use cheap chaff as early deployment drops to encourage the opponent to place important units first. Then place your key units against the matchups you want.
nieuw.waarom: He says that without these spare drops, you can be forced to reveal your key pieces before the opponent commits theirs.
nieuw.voorbeeld: He describes deploying a Wood Elf Beast Pack with a handler and two beasts early to use up a drop and make the opponent place another unit.

bronnen.citaat: And you put them down early, essentially wasting one of your drops.

extraCitaten.citaat: force your opponent to put a unit down.

nieuw.titel: Use threatening decoys to divert resources from your main threats
nieuw.tekst: Put chaff with real damage potential where it threatens something the opponent wants to protect. Make the opponent choose between spending resources to kill the decoy and letting it attack.
nieuw.waarom: He says that resources spent dealing with decoys are resources not spent dealing with your bigger threats, buying those threats time.
nieuw.voorbeeld: He pushed a Goblin Wolf Chariot forward to threaten Outriders and possibly bait Demigryph Knights. He describes it taking punishment while his Wyvern survived another turn and got the charge it needed.

bronnen.citaat: Your opponent has to pour resources into dealing with them.

extraCitaten.citaat: make your opponent decide whether to waste time killing it

nieuw.titel: Use Goblin Wolf Chariots to hunt artillery
nieuw.tekst: The speaker recommends Goblin Wolf Chariots as artillery hunters. If the opponent leaves one free, send it after a war machine.
nieuw.waarom: He points to their speed and the threat their impact hits pose to artillery with little armour.
nieuw.voorbeeld: When an enemy Griffon charged his Orc Boar Boy Mob instead of dealing with the Goblin Wolf Chariot, the chariot reached a mortar and destroyed it in one turn.

bronnen.citaat: Wolf chariots are great artillery hunters.

extraCitaten.citaat: he gets into a mortar and smashes it in one turn.

nieuw.titel: Cover a speed bump's overrun route with a countercharge
nieuw.tekst: Position a supporting unit to cover where the enemy will overrun after killing your speed bump. If the overrun leaves the enemy within reach, the support unit can countercharge it.
nieuw.voorbeeld: He says he should have wheeled his Orc Boar Chariot further to cover the area where the Skin Wolves would overrun after killing his Goblin Wolf Rider Mob.

bronnen.citaat: the Boar Chariot is able to countercharge the unit

nieuw.titel: Bait frenzied charges at maximum range, then flee
nieuw.tekst: Place chaff near the edge of a frenzied unit's charge range, make it charge, then flee and try to rally. The speaker particularly likes swift stride for this; make sure the enemy has no other unit to redirect into.
nieuw.waarom: He says the aim is to create space for the rest of your army to operate.
nieuw.wanneerNiet: He says fleeing is a waste if the opponent can redirect the charge into another unit.

nieuw.titel: Set up Wild Riders to charge Grail Knights without countercharge
nieuw.tekst: Against Grail Knights, use a Great Eagle to disrupt their movement so Wild Riders can charge without being countercharged. This is how the speaker sets up the matchup rather than relying on a straight fight.
nieuw.waarom: He says his force would not win that matchup in a straight fight and needed to disrupt the Grail Knights' movement to improve its chances.
nieuw.voorbeeld: His Great Eagle drew the Grail Knights into an overrun. The Wild Riders eventually charged, and he says the charge, a flank charge and the Waywatchers brought down the Grail Knights over two turns.
